# Example datasets

Two example datasets ship with the package, one per station type. They
are raw station exports, before any processing.


# Internal helpers

Small internal tools shared by every function of the package:

- **verbosity**: every exported function has `verbose = 0/1/2`
  (silent / summary / details). Messages go through `ppt_msg()`.
- **input checks**: `as_dt()` always returns a copy, so user objects are
  never modified; `check_cols()` reports missing columns.
- **per-pig fitting**: `fit_by_pig()` runs a function on each pig. A pig
  that fails is recorded and skipped instead of stopping everything.
- **removal log**: `new_removed()` builds the `removed` table returned by
  every analysis step.
- **result object**: `new_ppt_result()` gives every `calc_*()` function the
  same return structure.


# qc_config

All quality-control thresholds live in one object created by `qc_config()`.
Three presets are available, and any single parameter can be overridden.

```{r example-qc_config}
# Default preset
qc <- qc_config()
qc$duration_max

# Another preset with one parameter overridden
qc_national <- qc_config("national", min_test_days = 50)
qc_national

# Optional rules are off (NULL) unless switched on
qc_config("casey", daily_drop_min = 0.90)$daily_drop_min
```



# read_station

`read_station()` reads one or many station export files (or a whole
folder) and stacks them into one table. Columns are checked against the
station type, transponder IDs are always read as text so leading zeros are
kept, and a `source_file` column records where each row came from.

```{r example-read_station}
# Write the example data to two CSV files, then read them back
folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "fire_export")
dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 101, ], file.path(folder, "fire_101.csv"))
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 102, ], file.path(folder, "fire_102.csv"))

raw <- read_station(folder)
table(raw$source_file)
attr(raw, "station")

unlink(folder, recursive = TRUE)
```



# prep_visits

`prep_visits()` turns a raw NEDAP or FIRE export into one standard visit
table that every later step uses:

- one row per visit, **including unidentified visits** (no transponder
  read), marked with `identified = FALSE`. They are needed to compute the
  differences between subsequent visits on a feeder (Casey et al. 2005);
- the same column names and units for both stations: body weight in kg,
  feed intake and trough weights in g, times as POSIXct (UTC);
- FIRE visits that cross midnight get the right exit time;
- a body weight of 0 becomes `NA`;
- pigs seen at more than one station are kept (see **Station transfer**).

```{r example-prep_visits}
visits <- prep_visits(fire)
head(visits)

# Unidentified visits are kept for the feeder error checks
table(visits$identified)

# Station history of each pig
head(attr(visits, "stations"))

# NEDAP data gets the same columns and units
nedap_visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
summary(nedap_visits$weight)
```



# add_breed

Pig breed (or line) usually is not in the station export and cannot be
read from the transponder number. `add_breed()` merges a breed table from
your own records into the visit table. With a `breed` column:

- `calc_adfi()` adds breed as a fixed effect to the correction model;
- `fiv_max_by_weight` limits can differ by breed;
- `calc_fcr()` summarises traits by breed.

```{r example-add_breed}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
# a breed table from your own herd records, one row per pig
pigs <- unique(visits[identified == TRUE, responder])
breeds <- data.frame(responder = pigs, breed = rep(c("YY", "LL"), length.out = length(pigs)))
visits <- add_breed(visits, breeds)
table(unique(visits[identified == TRUE, .(responder, breed)])$breed)
```



# clean_weight

`clean_weight()` cleans the body weight records of identified visits in
three layers:

1. **record rules**: weights outside `weight_range` are flagged;
2. **outlier detection per pig**: one or more methods fit a curve to each
   pig and flag records far from it:
   - `"rlm"`: quadratic robust regression with bisquare weights
     (`MASS::rlm`), records with weight below `rlm_cutoff` are outliers;
   - `"loess"`: robust LOESS (`family = "symmetric"`), residuals beyond
     `sd_max` robust SDs;
   - `"stl"`: STL decomposition of the daily median weight (weekly
     period, robust), residuals beyond `sd_max` robust SDs. Falls back to
     LOESS for pigs with fewer than 14 days;
   - `"sd"`: quadratic least squares, residuals beyond `sd_max` SDs;
   - optional `rel_dev_max` and `daily_drop_min` rules;
3. **pig checks**: number of valid records, test length, missing rate,
   entry and exit weight, and optionally the curve R².

Nothing is deleted silently: every record keeps a `qc_flag`, and every
removed pig is listed in `removed` with the reason.

```{r example-clean_weight}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits)
w

# Why pigs were removed
w$removed

# Records flagged as outliers
head(w$records[outlier == TRUE])

# Another QC preset
w_national <- clean_weight(visits, qc = qc_config("national"), verbose = 0)
table(w_national$per_pig$status)
```



# calc_adg

`calc_adg()` estimates average daily gain (ADG) over the body weight stage
`stage_range` (default 30-120 kg):

1. a growth curve is fitted to the valid weight records of each pig
   (`curve_model`: polynomial, robust LOESS or Gompertz; Gompertz falls back
   to a quadratic curve when it does not converge);
2. the stage end is the first time the curve reaches the upper stage
   weight; the stage start is the **last** time the curve rises through the
   lower stage weight before that. A curve that dips back below 30 kg (for
   example after noisy early records) therefore starts the stage only once
   the pig has really entered it. The search runs up to `max_extrap_days`
   before the first and after the last record;
3. ADG = weight difference / days between these two times.

Every pig gets an `adg_type`:

- `"observed"`: both stage limits are reached inside the recorded period;
- `"extrapolated"`: at least one limit needs extrapolation, but no more
  than `max_extrap_days`;
- `"partial"`: a limit is not reached even after extrapolation. ADG is then
  the mean slope of the curve over the part of the stage that is covered;
- `"none"`: less than 7 days of the stage are covered; ADG is `NA`.

```{r example-calc_adg}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)
adg <- calc_adg(w)
head(adg$per_pig[, .(responder, adg_type, start_date, end_date, stage_days, adg)])

# Gompertz curve, with quadratic fallback
adg_g <- calc_adg(w, qc = qc_config("casey", curve_model = "gompertz"), verbose = 0)
table(adg_g$per_pig$curve_used)
```



# flag_feed_errors

`flag_feed_errors()` applies the 16 error criteria of Casey et al. (2005,
Table 3) to every visit.

The seven variables are computed on the **complete visit sequence of each
feeder**, including unidentified visits, sorted by entrance time:

- FIV = feed intake per visit (g), OTV = occupation time (s),
  FRV = FIV / (OTV / 60) (g/min, not computed when OTV <= 0);
- LWD = trough weight at entrance of the following visit - at exit of
  this visit; FWD = trough weight at entrance of this visit - at exit of the
  preceding visit (FIRE only, NEDAP has no trough weights);
- LTD = entrance time of the following visit - exit time of this visit;
  FTD = entrance time of this visit - exit time of the preceding visit.

| # | Error | Visits considered | Threshold (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | FIV-lo | all | FIV < -20 g |
| 2 | FIV-hi | all | FIV > 2000 g |
| 3 | FIV-0 | OTV = 0 | \|FIV\| > 20 g |
| 4 | OTV-lo | all | OTV < 0 s |
| 5 | OTV-hi | all | OTV > 3600 s |
| 6 | FRV-hi-FIV-lo | 0 < FIV < 50 g | FRV > 500 g/min |
| 7 | FRV-hi-strict | FIV >= 50 g, preceding or following visit FIV < -20 g | FRV > 110 g/min |
| 8 | FRV-hi | FIV >= 50 g, neither neighbour FIV < -20 g | FRV > 170 g/min |
| 9 | FRV-0 | FRV = 0 | OTV > 500 s |
| 10 | FRV-lo | FRV != 0 | \|FRV\| <= 2 g/min |
| 11-12 | LWD-lo / LWD-hi | all but the last visit on the feeder | LWD < -20 g / > 1800 g |
| 13-14 | FWD-lo / FWD-hi | all but the first visit on the feeder | FWD < -20 g / > 1800 g |
| 15 | LTD-lo | all but the last visit | LTD < 0 s |
| 16 | FTD-lo | all but the first visit | FTD < 0 s |

The thresholds come from [qc_config()]. Feed disappearance in unidentified
visits (-20 g <= FIV <= 2000 g) is summed per feeder; Casey et al. discarded
pens above 90 kg, here a warning is given above `max_unidentified_feed_kg`.

```{r example-flag_feed_errors}
visits <- prep_visits(fire, verbose = 0)
flagged <- flag_feed_errors(visits, verbose = 2)
attr(flagged, "feeders")
```



# calc_adfi

`calc_adfi()` estimates average daily feed intake (ADFI) over the same body
weight stage as [calc_adg()], so that FCR compares like with like.

**Correction** (Jiao et al. 2014, after Casey et al. 2005): for each pig and
day, the error-free intake `y` (sum of FIV over visits without error) is
modelled with a linear mixed model fitted on **all** pig-days:

`y ~ location + breed + BW + ADG + 16 x PTE + 11 x OTD + 4 x FID + (1 | pig)`

- PTE: share of the day's visits with error type p; OTD: occupation time
  of visits with error p (types 1, 2, 6-14); FID: feed intake of visits
  with error p (types 4, 5, 15, 16);
- BW: predicted body weight of the day from [calc_adg()]; ADG of the pig;
- `location` is a fixed effect when there is more than one station, and
  `breed` when the data have a `breed` column (see [add_breed()]) with
  more than one breed.

The corrected intake is `y - sum(b x error covariates)`: only the effects
of the error covariates are removed, so a day without errors keeps its
recorded intake. Covariates without variation or perfectly collinear with
others are dropped before fitting. Days on which every visit has an error
have no error-free intake and are imputed.

**Checks and imputation** over the stage days of each pig:

- corrected intake below 0, outside `dfi_range`, or outside the optional
  `dfi_quantile` limits is set to missing;
- `impute_method = "linear"` (default): linear interpolation inside the
  recorded period (`"iii"`), robust LOESS for gaps longer than
  `long_gap_days`, and a per-pig regression of intake on body weight
  outside the recorded period (`"elrp"`);
- `impute_method = "loess"`: a robust LOESS of daily intake over days,
  used both inside and outside the recorded period.

A simulation on the example data (random gaps, long gaps, late entry,
early exit) found no curve better than the others in every situation:
precision depends mainly on how many days are missing at the stage ends,
which is why such pigs are flagged by [calc_fcr()].

Day states: `"org"` (no error, recorded value), `"corr"` (corrected),
`"iii"` (interpolated), `"elrp"` (extrapolated), `"missing"`.

```{r example-calc_adfi}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)
adg <- calc_adg(w, verbose = 0)
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, adg)
head(adfi$per_pig)
table(adfi$daily[in_stage == TRUE, state])
head(adfi$model)
```



# calc_fcr

`calc_fcr()` combines ADG and ADFI, both computed over the same body weight
stage, into the feed conversion ratio FCR = ADFI / ADG (kg feed per kg
gain) and its inverse, feed efficiency G:F = ADG / ADFI.

Each pig gets `fcr_flag = "ok"` or `"low_confidence"`, with the reasons in
`fcr_note`: the growth curve or the feed intake extrapolated over more
than `max_edge_extrap_days` (default 15) at the start or end of the stage,
an inner 10 kg class with recorded weights spanning less than
`min_bin_coverage_kg` (default 6 kg), a segment FCR outside the optional
`bin_fcr_limits`,
ADG on part of the stage only, less than `min_coverage` (default 0.7) of
the stage with recorded feed intake, or weight data flagged by
[clean_weight()].

```{r example-calc_fcr}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
adg <- calc_adg(clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, adg, verbose = 0)
fcr <- calc_fcr(adg, adfi)
head(fcr$per_pig[, .(responder, adg, adfi, fcr, fcr_flag, fcr_note)])
fcr$summary[group == "all"]
```



# plot_adg, plot_adfi and save_plots

One plot per station, one panel per pig. Axes adapt to the data and to
`stage_range`, so no point is dropped. Colours come from a colour-blind safe
palette (Okabe-Ito) without extra packages.

```{r example-plots}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)
adg <- calc_adg(w, verbose = 0)
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, adg, verbose = 0)

g <- plot_adg(adg, weight = w, locations = "101", responders = c("13913", "13918", "13954"))
g$plot[[1]]

f <- plot_adfi(adfi, responders = c("13913", "13918", "13954"))
f$plot[[1]]

out <- save_plots(g, path = tempdir(), prefix = "loc", suffix = "growth", device = "pdf")
file.exists(out$file)
unlink(out$file)
```



# run_pipeline

`run_pipeline()` runs every step with one set of QC settings and keeps all
intermediate results.

```{r example-run_pipeline}
res <- run_pipeline(fire, qc = qc_config(stage_range = c(60, 120)), verbose = 0)
res
res$fcr$summary[group == "all"]
```



# write_results

`write_results()` writes the tables of an analysis to CSV files named
`<farm>_<table>_<date>.csv`, ready to send to the testing station. Files
are UTF-8 with a byte order mark so that Excel shows Chinese text correctly.

```{r example-write_results}
res <- run_pipeline(nedap, verbose = 0)
out <- write_results(res, dir = file.path(tempdir(), "results"), farm = "demo")
out
unlink(file.path(tempdir(), "results"), recursive = TRUE)
```



# validate_outliers, validate_adg and validate_adfi

Three functions check how well the methods work **on your own data**, by
hiding or spoiling part of the data on purpose and measuring how close the
result comes to what is known:

- `validate_outliers()` adds artificial errors to clean weight records and
  measures how many each outlier method finds, how many good records it
  removes, and how much ADG is affected;
- `validate_adg()` compares growth curve models by k-fold cross-validation on
  recorded days, and by how much ADG changes when the first or last days of
  the test are hidden (late entry, early exit);
- `validate_adfi()` hides recorded feed intake days (random days, blocks,
  start or end of the stage), imputes them again and compares ADFI with the
  recorded value.

```{r example-validate}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)

# 1. weight outlier methods: 5% artificial errors of 3-15 kg
vo <- validate_outliers(visits, reps = 1)
vo$summary

# 2. growth curve models
va <- validate_adg(w, models = c("poly1", "poly2", "loess"))
va$summary

# 3. feed intake imputation
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, calc_adg(w, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
vf <- validate_adfi(adfi, scenarios = c("random30", "late20"), reps = 2)
vf$summary
```
